stage1.impression: A clean, evenly lit CG interior: a staggered record wall fills the left half and a glowing ice-blue horn speaker sits on a black plinth at right, with flat brown walls and a pale concrete floor. Exposure and light are flat. It reads as dusk-to-daylight, not as a kissa bar at night lit by its own acrylic. The speaker's cyan interior looks self-lit and cut out against the room, the record spines repeat in obvious stripe patterns, and the walls have no texture, so it reads as a render rather than an interiors photograph.

blocking_9: The room must read as night: walls and floor fall well below the speaker, with light pooling from named sources, not a flat ambient fill
The speaker's own colour must spill onto the plinth, the floor and the wall behind it, so it sits in the room rather than on it
The frame must show what the card asks for: the lounge's low chairs in front and the pair either side of the record wall, not one speaker and a wall of shelves
The record spines must stop reading as a procedural stripe texture: they need varied widths, slight leans, worn edges and some sleeves pulled out
The walls and floor need real material micro-detail (plaster or concrete with tooling, the floor's honing and sheen) and no flat CG brown
The plinth's bottom edge needs uncropped breathing room and a contact shadow with a soft falloff

defects.what: the walls are a flat, untextured brown plane; they darken downward (101 to 52 lum top to bottom) as if lit from the ceiling only, with no wash or pool from the speaker or spots

the floor (lum ~125) is brighter than the walls (~75-88): this reads as daylight or overhead fill, not a night bar; its texture is mottled and low-contrast with no reflections of the speaker or the shelves
the record spines are uniform-width stripe patterns with obvious repetition between cubbies and no wear or lean; they are the brightest, busiest region and compete with the hero
the shelf units step in height (staggered bottoms at y~690-720) and read as floating modules; there are no visible edge-lit shelf strips glowing
the cyan batts glow at ~165-190 lum while nothing nearby takes their colour: the floor beside the plinth measures r126 g115 b95, so no blue spill; it reads as emissive and pasted on
the horn reads as a dark, murky slab (median lum 39) with a black blob at the throat; it loses the tinted-resin read
the plinth is cropped by the bottom edge; its glossy black top mirrors the cyan but its base has no soft contact shadow on the floor
there are no chairs, props or people: the card's lounge is missing from the frame, there is no scale cue, and there is no depth from foreground to background
the right-hand wall corner is a dead, dark wedge with no light

changes.problem: The room is flatly lit and brighter on the floor than on the walls, so it does not read as a bar at night lit by its acrylic.

evidence.measured: floor lum_median 129 against walls 88 (560-760,50-300) and 74 (1050-1190,50-400); wall falloff 101 to 52 top to bottom

changes.expected: The ambient floor and walls drop by about a stop; the speaker's glow and the spots carry the frame.

changes.problem: The speaker does not light its surroundings: no blue on the floor, the plinth or the wall behind.

evidence.measured: floor by the plinth r126 g115 b95: no cyan component

change.setting: lamps: the wash behind each pair
change.from: 4 x spot, 90 W, cone 50 deg, white
change.to: 4 x spot, 140 W, cone 60 deg, tinted to the Ice cabinet colour (about #5FC8E0) and aimed at the wall and floor behind the speaker; also drop the on-speaker area lamps from 12 to 8 W/m2 so the interior reads lit from within, not floodlit

changes.expected: A soft cyan halo on the wall behind the speaker and a cool pool on the floor around the plinth.

changes.problem: The frame misses its brief: no lounge chairs and only one of the pair; the record wall's busy spines take half the frame and outshout the speaker.

evidence.measured: record wall median 138 with p95 229, brighter than the speaker body (~110-165), occupying 44% of the width

change.to: position [13.6, 2.6, 1.05], target [17.6, 4.57, 0.85], 28 mm, f/2.8 focused on the near speaker: a low chair in the soft foreground, the near speaker at right third, the record wall centred behind and the second speaker at left edge

changes.expected: Foreground to background depth, both of the pair, and a hierarchy with the speaker as hero. No pixel test, because the camera moves.

changes.problem: The record wall is lit evenly and brightly, so it reads as a flat wallpaper texture and competes with the hero.

evidence.measured: lum_median 138, p95 229, the highest-energy region in the frame

change.setting: lamps: the record wall and shelves
change.from: record wall 3 x spot 60 W cone 45 deg; shelves 0.15
change.to: record wall 3 x spot 30 W cone 25 deg (grazing from above, leaving pools); shelves 0.35 so the edge-lit shelf lines read as the light source

changes.expected: Spines in pools and falloff, with glowing shelf edges; the wall drops below the speaker in brightness.

changes.problem: The walls are flat brown CG planes with no surface.

evidence.measured: lum_range 26.6, a smooth gradient with no micro-texture

change.to: a dark lime plaster or board-formed concrete, base #3A332C, roughness 0.85, with a 2-4 mm trowel or formwork bump map and 6-10% albedo variation

changes.expected: The walls take grazing light with visible tooling; the speaker's cyan wash reveals texture.

changes.problem: The floor is a matte, mottled concrete with no sheen, so nothing reflects and there is no sense of a finished bar floor.

evidence.measured: lum_range 19.1, no reflection of the speaker or the shelves

change.to: honed and sealed concrete, roughness 0.35, darker base #6E665C, fine aggregate and a few saw joints

changes.expected: Soft, blurred reflections of the cyan cabinet and the shelf glow on the floor.

changes.problem: The record spines read as a procedural stripe texture repeated across cubbies.

evidence.measured: visible in the crop: uniform stripe widths and repeated colour sequences, with no lean or pulled sleeves

change.from: a striped spine texture per cubby
change.to: individual sleeves with spine widths of 3-6 mm, ±3 deg lean, a few faced-out covers and two or three sleeves half-pulled, with randomized per-cubby seeds and a muted palette (desaturate 25%)

changes.expected: The wall reads as a real collection, not wallpaper.

changes.problem: The room is empty: there are no chairs, glasses or haze, so there is no scale cue and no sense of a bar.

evidence.measured: the haze at 0.008/m has no visible effect: the wall gradient is smooth and there are no visible beams

change.from: no lounge props in frame; haze 0.008
change.to: a low lounge chair and side table with a rocks glass in the soft foreground; haze 0.02/m, anisotropy 0.5, so the spots and the speaker glow show faint volume

changes.expected: Depth, scale and the night-bar atmosphere.

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn read more clearly as tinted resin (it renders as a dark, murky slab with a black throat).
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's own material and shape, which are fixed; c2 and c4 may let more light pass through it.

out_of_scope.request: Show the white batts less cyan-saturated.
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's colour and parts, which are fixed.

out_of_scope.request: Align the staggered shelf-unit bottoms of the record wall.
out_of_scope.why: The record wall's design is fixed as proposed.
